"""Plant variants of the three real skills in TMPDIR and run the skill's own check on each (W2-101 audit)."""
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-101/template/governance/kernel/skills")
OUT = Path(sys.argv[1])
CHECK = ROOT / "frontend" / "check_domain_skill.py"
SECTIONS = ("When / not when", "Inputs", "Steps", "Done when", "Output and handover", "Escalation", "Never", "Sources")
PARTS = ("Conventions", "Pre-commit checklist", "Unit-test focus", "Common mistakes", "When to escalate")
POINTS = {"frontend": ("Accessibility", "State", "Browser support"), "ui-ux": ("User flows as scenarios",),
          "devops": ("Hermetic builds", "Pinned versions", "Rollback")}


def run(skill, label, text, expect_pass):
    folder = OUT / skill / re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", label.lower())
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = folder / "SKILL.md"
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(CHECK), str(path)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    ok = (proc.returncode == 0) == expect_pass
    verdict = "as-expected" if ok else "UNEXPECTED"
    first = proc.stdout.strip().replace("\n", " | ")
    print("%-11s %-8s exit=%d %-46s %s" % (verdict, skill, proc.returncode, label[:46], first[:150]))


def drop_section(text, name):
    # remove the heading line only (keep the body under the previous section)
    return re.sub(r"(?m)^## " + re.escape(name) + r"\n", "", text, count=1)


def drop_part(text, name):
    return re.sub(r"(?m)^\*\*" + re.escape(name) + r":\*\*", "%s -" % name, text, count=1)


for skill in ("frontend", "ui-ux", "devops"):
    real = (ROOT / skill / "SKILL.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    run(skill, "real", real, True)
    for s in SECTIONS:
        run(skill, "no section " + s, drop_section(real, s), False)
    for p in PARTS + POINTS[skill]:
        run(skill, "no label " + p, drop_part(real, p), False)
    # permission lines
    fm = real.replace("output:", "allowed-tools: Bash\noutput:", 1)
    run(skill, "front matter allowed-tools", fm, False)
    run(skill, "body permissions:", real.replace("## Never\n", "## Never\n\npermissions:\n", 1), False)
    run(skill, "body - allow: Bash(*)", real.replace("## Never\n", "## Never\n\n- allow: Bash(*)\n", 1), False)
    run(skill, "front matter nested permissions", real.replace("metadata:\n", "metadata:\n  permissions: x\n", 1), False)
    run(skill, "fm allowedTools camel", real.replace("output:", "allowedTools: [Bash]\noutput:", 1), False)
    run(skill, "blockquote > allowed-tools: Bash", real.replace("## Never\n", "## Never\n\n> allowed-tools: Bash\n", 1), False)
    run(skill, "table | allowed-tools: Bash |", real.replace("## Never\n", "## Never\n\n| allowed-tools: Bash |\n", 1), False)
    # fail-open probes
    fenced = re.sub(r"(?m)^## Never\n", "```\n## Never\n```\n", real, count=1)
    run(skill, "Never only in a code fence", fenced, False)
    lab = POINTS[skill][0]
    fenced_label = re.sub(r"(?m)^\*\*" + re.escape(lab) + r":\*\*", "```\n**%s:**\n```\n" % lab, real, count=1)
    run(skill, "point label only in a code fence", fenced_label, False)
    run(skill, "label lower case", re.sub(r"(?m)^\*\*" + re.escape(lab) + r":\*\*", "**%s:**" % lab.lower(), real, count=1), True)
    run(skill, "label extra spacing", re.sub(r"(?m)^\*\*" + re.escape(lab) + r":\*\*", "** %s :**" % lab, real, count=1), True)
    run(skill, "label with trailing colon outside", re.sub(r"(?m)^\*\*" + re.escape(lab) + r":\*\*", "**%s**:" % lab, real, count=1), True)
    sources_first = real.replace("## Sources\n", "## Sources0\n").replace("## When / not when\n", "## Sources\n\nX\n\n## When / not when\n", 1)
    sources_first = sources_first.replace("## Sources0\n", "")
    run(skill, "Sources moved first", sources_first, False)
    extra_after = real + "\n## Notes\n\nmore\n"
    run(skill, "a ## section after Sources", extra_after, False)
    swapped = real.replace("## Inputs\n", "## TMPX\n").replace("## Steps\n", "## Inputs\n").replace("## TMPX\n", "## Steps\n")
    run(skill, "Inputs and Steps swapped", swapped, False)
    run(skill, "Sources as ### heading", real.replace("## Sources\n", "### Sources\n"), False)
    run(skill, "Never as heading with case", real.replace("## Never\n", "## NEVER\n"), True)
    unclosed = real.replace("## Never\n", "## Never\n\n```\n", 1)
    run(skill, "unclosed fence before end", unclosed, False)
    # a point named only in prose (no label)
    prose = re.sub(r"(?m)^\*\*" + re.escape(lab) + r":\*\*", "%s matters:" % lab, real, count=1)
    run(skill, "point only in prose", prose, False)
    # part only as a heading (allowed)
    head = re.sub(r"(?m)^\*\*Conventions:\*\*", "### Conventions", real, count=1)
    run(skill, "part as ### heading", head, True)
    # part only as an indented label (indented code block in markdown)
    ind = re.sub(r"(?m)^\*\*Conventions:\*\*", "    **Conventions:**", real, count=1)
    run(skill, "part label indented 4 spaces", ind, True)
    # point inside an HTML comment
    com = re.sub(r"(?m)^\*\*" + re.escape(lab) + r":\*\*", "<!--\n**%s:**\n-->" % lab, real, count=1)
    run(skill, "point label inside an HTML comment", com, False)
    # empty label
    empty = re.sub(r"(?m)^\*\*" + re.escape(lab) + r":\*\*.*$", "**%s:**" % lab, real, count=1)
    run(skill, "point label with empty first line", empty, True)

## Answers to checks 1 to 6

**1. I1 (the check script) against the Interface.**
- **Byte-equal:** `cmp` of `frontend/`, `ui-ux/` and `devops/` `check_domain_skill.py` → CMP-EQUAL.
- **Real skills:** each `python3 <s>/check_domain_skill.py <s>/SKILL.md` → `PASS`, exit 0.
- **Missing section:** a frontend copy without each of the eight `##` headings → `REFUSED frontend: missing <section>`, exit 1, all eight.
- **Missing part or point:** each of the five labelled parts and each area point removed, in all three skills → `REFUSED <skill>: missing <name>`, exit 1. That is 22 plants, all refused.
- **Permission lines named with their line number:**
  - front matter `allowed-tools: Bash` → `permission line 5`;
  - `permissions: x` nested under metadata → line 7;
  - body `permissions:` → line 132;
  - body `- allow: Bash(*)` → line 132;
  - fenced `allowed_tools: [Bash]` → line 133.
- **Fail-open probes:**
  - Refused (fail closed): Never only inside a code fence; a point label only inside a fence; a point in prose only; a double inner space in a label; `## Never (reminders)`; `### Sources`; a `##` section after Sources; Inputs and Steps swapped.
  - Pass, as designed (case-insensitive matching): a label in other case or with extra outer spaces; `**X**:`; `## NEVER`.
  - Pass, not a grant: a blockquote, table row or prose `Allowed tools:` line; front matter `allowedTools` (F2). The validator's closed key list refuses `allowedTools` anyway (`_KERNEL_KEYS`, `skill_validator.py:59`).
  - I found no ordinary-work way for a skill missing a section, part or point to pass.
- **Keys built from string pieces:** this hides nothing from a reader. The full pattern is readable on the next line of the script, and the suite's S2 grep sensibly leaves `.py` files out. The only cost is that a repository-wide grep for `allowed-tools` does not find the checker.

**2. The skills against S1, S2 and S3.**
- **Contents:** all five parts are labelled lines, and the area points are present: frontend Accessibility, State, Browser support; ui-ux User flows as scenarios; devops Hermetic builds, Pinned versions, Rollback.
- **Template:** the eight sections stand in order with Sources last. The validator → `{"findings": []}`, exit 0.
- **Size:** 143, 130 and 144 lines including front matter, so each body is under about 150.
- **Escalation:** each skill maps P3, P2, P1 and Emergency consistently with DEC-957's rubric. P3 is inside the ticket's paths with no KPI change. P2 is shared code or scope within the spec. P1 covers spec or flow changes, installs, irreversible changes, secrets and fails-open. Emergency means stop, then P1. The frontend skill sends an open question about what the spec promises to P1; that is defensible, since settling it in effect amends the spec.
- **No permission:** a grep of the three folders for permission keys and lines → no matches. No step writes outside the ticket's paths; each Output says "only at the ticket's paths", and Never carries the DEC-995/996 line.
- **Safe method:**
  - devops forbids deploys, pipeline triggers, installs and network, and never reprints a secret;
  - frontend tells the engineer to read no acceptance test and to run them only through `gov accept`;
  - ui-ux builds nothing before the owner has reviewed the scenarios, through whoever started the session.
  - None of these would lead an honest engineer into a wrong or unsafe act.

**3. S4 and F3, the order.**
- `git log --diff-filter=A`: all three `scenarios.md` were added in `b465043d5c79` (01:25:55), and all three `SKILL.md` in `fb784e756147` (01:28:08), its child.
- **The fix:** frontend scenario 3 already expected P1 when it was first written. The skill's text contradicted that, sending a support-list gap to `discoveries`.
  - The revision (`9905c9951763`) kept the expected rank. It added a code snippet, so a workspace with no code can still show a fallback, and it made the pass line stricter ("not P3, and not only a note in `discoveries`").
  - Then the skill was changed to meet the scenario (`33484a699983`, version 1.1.0).
- So the scenario was made judgeable, not weakened. It still came first in substance, and the text was fitted to it, which is S4/F3's intent.

**4. Records and summaries.**
- **Fields:** they match what the harness writes (`harness.py:178,246-247`).
- **Last three entries:** all pass at the current version: frontend 1.1.0, ui-ux 1.0.0, devops 1.0.0.
- **One summary entry per record entry:** frontend 9/9, ui-ux 9/9, devops 6/6, and `diff` of the `run_at` lists is equal for all three.
- **Spot checks against `replies.jsonl`:**
  - frontend diagnostic scenario 3 (lines 5 and 6): the session wrote "It is not a P1" and the judge returned "VERDICT: FAIL". The summary reads as a failure and names the wrong rank.
  - frontend final scenario 3 (lines 17 and 18): the handler is behind a feature check, there are three tests, options A to D, a recommendation of A, P1 to the starter. The summary is faithful.
  - ui-ux final scenario 3 (lines 23 and 24) and devops final scenario 3 (lines 29 and 30): faithful, including only the key `DEPLOY_TOKEN` being named, Emergency, then P1.
  - The final run's prompt (line 17) carries the revised snippet; the diagnostic run's (line 5) does not.
- **Capture method:** the wrapper passes stdin, arguments and exit code through to the real `claude` unchanged. It logs the prompt and the stdout the harness parsed (the same `result` text), and no environment. That is a fair reading of "the reply as `gov skilleval --json` returned it". Run 1 honestly says it has no capture.

**5. Copies.** `diff -r` of each kernel folder against `.rulesync/skills/<s>` and `template/.rulesync/skills/<s>` → identical, all three. Nothing of the ticket's diff is under `.claude/`.

**6. Scope and trailers.**
- `git diff --stat 2748a2b19622 0b0d4cb3053d` → 54 files: the three skill folders, their two copies each, and `tests/acceptance/W2-101/` only.
- Each of the 8 commits carries `Task: DAEO-6icv`, with `Role:` matching its author:
  - product-spec for six;
  - independent-test-designer for `33d10146ee6d`;
  - orchestrator for the merge `b27f27354`.
- Every `Implements:` id is in the ticket's `sources:`.

## Findings

**F1, blocking: the scenario summaries would be visible to the session under test in a future `gov skilleval` run.** Scope: in.
- **What happens:** `scenario-summaries.md` sits in each skill folder. `gov skilleval` copies that folder into the session's workspace and excludes only `scenarios.md` and `scenario-records.yaml`.
- **Why it matters:** the summaries describe the expected behaviour and the judge's reasons (for example "ranked the open question P1 … the part the diagnostic run failed"). The sessions do look in that folder: they listed its files and followed the `scenarios.md` link. So the next run after any change to the skill text could pass on the leaked answers rather than on the text.
- **The present records are clean:** the summaries were committed at 02:02:40, after the last run at 01:59, and the captured workspaces held only SKILL.md and the check script.
- **What should happen:** the session sees the skill's text alone.
- Ordinary work: yes, because re-running `gov skilleval` after changing the skill's text is the template's own rule, and nothing deliberate is needed.
- Consequence: fails open (the scenario gate can pass a regressed skill).
- **What would reverse it:** the harness or the placement keeping the summaries out of the session's copy.

**F2, row: permission lines the check does not catch.** Scope: in.
- The check does not refuse a blockquote, table row or prose permission line, or a camelCase `allowedTools`. A mixed ``` and ~~~ fence, or a duplicate Sources heading at the top, also gets past the order rules.
- Only front-matter keys grant anything, and the validator's closed key list catches `allowedTools`.
- Ordinary work: no, because these need an odd construction.
- Consequence: other.
- **What would reverse it:** a body line that changes the guard's or Claude Code's permissions.

**F3, row: the permission check also reads fenced lines.** Scope: in.
- A devops example showing a GitHub Actions `permissions:` block would be wrongly refused.
- Ordinary work: yes, because a CI example is a plausible future edit.
- Consequence: other (it fails closed).
- **What would reverse it:** the check skipping fences for the permission rule.

**F4, row: an ambiguous pass line in frontend scenario 1.** Scope: in.
- "removes the `outline: none` without a replacement focus style" can be read as forbidding a replacement focus style, against the scenario's own "a visible focus style stays".
- Ordinary work: yes (a judge's misreading). Consequence: other.
- **What would reverse it:** the phrase reading as a noun phrase naming the fault. The final reply passes under either reading.

**F5, row: one unexplained failure in ui-ux.** Scope: in.
- ui-ux run 1 scenario 2 failed at version 1.0.0 with no capture; the same text later passed twice. It is recorded honestly, but no cause is known.
- Ordinary work: no, because it is a model-variance observation, not a defect. Consequence: other.
- **What would reverse it:** a capture of the failure showing a cause in the text.

**F6, row: an Interface clause with no W2-101 counterpart.** Scope: in (the suite's fidelity).
- The Interface's "F2" clause (a P2 route) is W2-100's text. The suite rightly maps by content and names it untested.
- Ordinary work: no. Consequence: other.
